## Description {#details}

C++ header file with declarations for the µTest++ type trait utilities and metaprogramming support.

This header provides the declarations for the type trait utilities and metaprogramming constructs used within the µTest++ framework. It defines templates and variable traits for function traits, type lists, identity, value wrappers, compile-time checks for container and floating-point types, and type convertibility.

These utilities underpin advanced template programming, type deduction, and compile-time introspection, supporting the flexible and type-safe design of the framework. The provided traits and wrappers enable expressive and generic handling of types, values, and callable objects, facilitating robust and maintainable test code.

All definitions reside within the <code><a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/type-traits">micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::type&#95;traits</a></code> namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.

All header files are organised within the <code>include/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus</code> folder to maintain a structured and modular codebase.

This file is intended for internal use within the framework and should not be included directly by user code.

### declval() {#ae488d06debb38c5e638355cb462a1228}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>T &amp;&amp; micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::type&#95;traits::declval (void)</>}>
Utility function template to simulate std::declval for type deduction.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">The type for which an rvalue reference is required.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<SectionUser title="Parameters">
None.
</SectionUser>


<SectionUser title="Returns">
An rvalue reference to type <code>T</code>.
</SectionUser>

The <code>declval</code> function template provides a mechanism for obtaining an rvalue reference to a type <code>T</code> without requiring an actual object. This is primarily used in unevaluated contexts, such as within <code>decltype</code>, to deduce types during template metaprogramming in the µTest++ framework.

Function template to determine if one type is convertible to another.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="From">The source type to be checked for convertibility.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="To">The target type to which conversion is tested.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

</ParametersList>
The <code>is&#95;convertible</code> function template checks, at compile time, whether a value of type <code>From</code> can be implicitly converted to type <code>To</code>. This is achieved using SFINAE and is primarily used as an implementation detail for the <code>is&#95;convertible&#95;v</code> variable template within the µTest++ framework.

If the conversion is valid, this overload is selected and returns <code>true</code>.

### is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v {#abfe0c2413694bb3a6dcdf1da303c38db}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>auto micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::type&#95;traits::is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v = false</>}
  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Variable template to determine if a type is a floating point type.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">The type to be checked for floating point classification.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<ParametersList title="Return Values">
<ParametersListItem name="true">if <code>T</code> is a floating point type.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="false">otherwise.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>
The <code>is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> is a floating point type (<code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, or <code>long double</code>). For all other types, it evaluates to <code>false</code>. This trait is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable type-safe handling and specialisation for floating point types in template metaprogramming.

Specialisations are provided for <code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, and <code>long double</code>, each evaluating to <code>true</code>.

Definition at line <a href="#l00465">465</a> of file <a href="/micro-test-plus-xpack/docs/api/files/include/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/type-traits-h">type-traits.h</a>.

Variable template specialisation indicating that <code>double</code> is a floating point type.
